If seeding the carrier ahead of the clamp leaves the count at 127 (still coalesced) or adds an instruction of its own for the seed, the carrier/quotient interference is not source-constructible here and the function should be typed-parked as a two-register role inversion with the `+1 b / -1 fmr` signature.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes - the target at +0x148/+0x14c loads the upper-bound constant into f1 and immediately compares `fcmpo cr0,f0,f1`, which is the observation that the carrier and the quotient are simultaneously live there and therefore cannot be coalesced; the seeded spelling itself has NOT been compiled.
hypothesis.statement: The target's shape is quotient-in-a-TEMP plus carrier-in-a-NAMED-LOCAL, and probe 3 proved the temp form is reachable - it only failed because nothing stopped MWCC coalescing the carrier with that temp. The untried lever is to make the two INTERFERE, so coalescing is illegal: keep the CSE (unnamed) quotient of probe 3 but give the carrier a live range that overlaps it, e.g. seed the carrier from the upper-bound constant BEFORE the first comparison (`clamped = lbl_80343BEC;` ahead of the `< pt01` test) so the carrier is live while the quotient is still being compared, exactly as the target has it at +0x14c (`fcmpo cr0,f0,f1` reads both registers at once).
